about: Reference list /grammar/phrasal-verbs-list (Spanish: reflexive and pronominal verbs; the `routes` item moves it to /grammar/reflexive-verbs-list). items: [verb, forms (yo presente · él indefinido · participio), example, level]; a string starting with '# ' is a sub-heading. Section ids are kept from the German list: trennbar = daily routine and the body, untrennbar = with a fixed preposition, beides = se changes the meaning, three-part = feelings and change. The worksheet builds sentences from the trennbar examples and the live quiz asks for the yo form with its pronoun, so every yo form starts with `me`. *…* in regel becomes bold.
title: Reflexive and pronominal verbs
metaTitle: Spanish reflexive and pronominal verbs: list with examples – Reference – icanspeak Spanish
description: Common Spanish reflexive and pronominal verbs with their forms and an example: daily routine, verbs with a fixed preposition, and verbs where se changes the meaning.
lead: Verbs that come with a pronoun: me, te, se, nos, os, se. Each one has its forms and an example. The rule is above each list.
practice: Verbs of change: ponerse, volverse, hacerse

sections.name: Daily routine and the body
sections.what: You do the action to yourself. The pronoun changes with the person: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta.
regel: The pronoun goes with the person: *me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, os levantáis, se levantan.*
It goes before a conjugated verb and after an infinitive or a gerund, written as one word: *Me voy a duchar. / Voy a ducharme.*
With the body and clothes, use the article, not a possessive: *Me lavo las manos.* (not *mis manos*)
In compound tenses it goes before *haber*: *Me he levantado tarde.*
items: Me quito los zapatos en casa.
Me mudo a Málaga en mayo.

sections.name: With a fixed preposition
sections.what: The preposition belongs to the verb. Learn the two together.
regel: The preposition is part of the verb: *acordarse de, atreverse a, fijarse en, casarse con.*
After it comes a noun, a pronoun or an infinitive: *Me acuerdo de Ana. Me acuerdo de ti. Me olvidé de llamar.*
The preposition stays before a *que* clause: *Me di cuenta de que era tarde.* (not *me di cuenta que*)
In questions the preposition goes first: *¿De qué te quejas?*
items: Me olvidé de llamar al casero.
Luis se casó con Marta en junio.
me doy cuenta · se dio cuenta · dado cuenta
Me di cuenta de que no tenía las llaves.
Me enteré de la noticia por la radio.
Los vecinos se quejan del ruido.
Me encontré con Luis en el metro.
Me parezco mucho a mi madre.
Me he acostumbrado a cenar tarde.
Fíjate en la fecha de la cita.

sections.name: se changes the meaning
sections.what: With or without the pronoun, these are almost two different verbs. The English in brackets shows the difference.
regel: *ir* says where you go, *irse* that you leave: *Voy a casa. / Me voy.*
*se* can add “completely”: *Comí tarta.* (some cake) / *Me comí la tarta.* (the whole cake)
Listen for the difference in *me siento*: it is the yo form of both *sentarse* (sit down) and *sentirse* (feel).
Some of these are very common in spoken Spain Spanish, so it is worth learning both meanings.
items: Me voy. (I'm leaving.) Voy a casa. (I'm going home.)
Me quedo en casa. (I'm staying.) Quedo con Ana. (I'm meeting Ana.)
Me dormí en el sofá. (I fell asleep.) Dormí bien. (I slept well.)
Me llevo este. (I'll take this one.) Llevo un abrigo. (I'm wearing a coat.)
Me comí la tarta. (the whole cake) Comí tarta. (some cake)
Me encuentro mal. (I feel ill.) Encuentro las llaves. (I find the keys.)
Me siento mal. (I feel ill.) Lo siento. (I'm sorry.)
Me bajo aquí. (I'm getting off here.) Bajo a la calle. (I'm going down to the street.)
Se despidió de todos. (He said goodbye.) Lo despidieron. (They fired him.)
Me niego a firmar. (I refuse to sign.) Lo niego. (I deny it.)
Me acuerdo de ti. (I remember you.) Acordamos el precio. (We agreed the price.)

sections.name: Feelings and change
sections.what: These say that a person's state changes: they get angry, get bored, fall in love. English often uses “get” or “become”.
regel: Feelings often use a pronominal verb: *Me enfado. Me aburro. Me alegro.*
A preposition often follows: *alegrarse de, enamorarse de, preocuparse por, enfadarse con.*
*ponerse* + adjective is a change for a while: *Me pongo nervioso.* *hacerse* and *convertirse en* are lasting changes: *Se hizo médica.*
items: Me enfadé con mi hermano. (Latin America: enojarse)
Me canso mucho en este trabajo.
Me pongo nervioso en los exámenes.
Me quedé dormido en el metro.
Con los años se hizo médica.
El pueblo se convirtió en una ciudad.
